title: github-project-bootstrap epics/stories data file
description: Portable replacement for tracker/issues.py's MILESTONE, EPICS, and RELEASE_VALIDATION_ISSUE module attributes, consumed by scripts/bootstrap_github_project.py via a --data <path.json> argument (see epic-schema.md). LIMITATION: this schema validates shape only (types, required fields, that `depends_on` is an array of strings). It cannot express the ordering constraint that every epics[].depends_on entry must name the `title` of an epic appearing at an earlier index in the `epics` array (never itself, never a later one) -- JSON Schema has no keyword that compares a value against sibling elements of another array by position. That constraint must be checked separately by the code that loads this file (see epic-schema.md's "What JSON Schema can validate here vs. what it can't" section); a schema-valid document can still violate it.

milestone.description: The single GitHub milestone every epic and issue is filed under. Looked up by title and reused if it already exists; created via `gh api POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/milestones` if not.

title.description: Exact milestone title, e.g. "v1 -- Four Skills Shipped & Shareable". Used both to look up an existing milestone and, via --milestone, as the value every created issue is filed under.

epics.description: Ordered list of epics, created as GitHub issues in array order. Order is load-bearing: see epic-schema.md's ordering-constraint section. Each epics[].depends_on entry must name the `title` of an epic that appears earlier in this same array -- a constraint this schema cannot enforce (see this schema's top-level `description`).

release_validation_issue.description: The single standalone issue created last and linked as blocked-by every epic issue. Same shape as a child issue (title/labels/body) -- it has no `depends_on` or `issues` of its own.

epic.description: One epic: created as an issue labeled `epic` plus any of its own `labels`, then its `issues` are created as GitHub sub-issues of it (`gh issue create --parent`).

title.description: Exact epic issue title, e.g. "Epic: Skill -- github-project-bootstrap". Referenced verbatim by other epics' `depends_on` entries, so it must match exactly wherever it's cited.

labels.description: Additional labels layered on top of the literal `epic` label the bootstrap script always adds. Optional; omitted or empty means no labels beyond `epic`.

depends_on.description: Titles of other epics this epic is blocked by (`gh issue edit --add-blocked-by`). Each title must exactly match another epic's `title` earlier in the enclosing `epics` array -- never this epic's own title, never a later epic's. Not enforceable by JSON Schema; see this schema's top-level `description`. Optional; omitted or empty means this epic has no epic-level blockers.

body.description: Issue body markdown for the epic.

issues.description: Child story issues, created as GitHub sub-issues of this epic. May be empty, but the key itself is required.

labeledIssue.description: A single leaf issue: a child story under an epic, or the top-level release_validation_issue.

labels.description: Additional labels. For a child issue under an epic, these are layered on top of the literal `task` label the bootstrap script always adds; release_validation_issue gets no such automatic label, so its `labels` list is applied as-is. Optional; omitted or empty means no additional labels.
